rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note K discloses an Antidumping (AD) and Countervailing Duty (CVD) Investigation by the US Department of Commerce against hardwood plywood imports from Vietnam assembled using Chinese cores. Two of AMWD's primary Vietnamese plywood vendors were on the ineligible-for-certification list in the DOC's July 2023 Final Determination, requiring 206% AD/CVD cash deposits. AMWD recorded a $4.9M loss in FY24 ($3.7M net of tax) for unliquidated customs entries. Subsequent disclosure: the Final Review found AMWD's two Vietnamese vendors ELIGIBLE for certification, and if not appealed by petitioners, DOC will issue refund instructions within 35 days and the deposits will be refunded within 6 months.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A + Mode B: verify the AD/CVD disclosure via EDGAR (Note K), assess whether the 206% deposit refund is a near-term tailwind, and whether the broader 2026-01-01 Trump-administration tariffs on softwood lumber / kitchen cabinets / bathroom vanities / upholstered wooden furniture compound or partially offset this Vietnamese supply chain.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note K), edgar_fts (broader tariff context), and 10-K Item 7 MD&A discussion of 2026-01-01 tariffs
rfm_tuples.M_value: AD/CVD timeline: Feb 2020 petition filed; Jul 2022 Preliminary Determination; Jul 2023 Final Determination put 2 of AMWD's primary Vietnamese plywood vendors on ineligible-for-certification list with 206% cash-deposit requirement; FY24 loss $4.9M / $3.7M net of tax recorded; Final Review (date not disclosed in the 10-K excerpt) FOUND the 2 vendors ELIGIBLE — if no petitioner appeal within ~35 days the deposits get refunded within 6 months. Separately, 2026-01-01 Trump-administration tariffs hit softwood lumber, kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, upholstered wooden furniture; February 20, 2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling struck down certain IEEPA tariffs but Section 301/232 tariffs persist (per original AMWD-07).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: MIXED — the AD/CVD Final Review is potentially a meaningful refund event (could be $5-10M of cash, possibly back into FY26/FY27 cash flow), and structurally the 2026-01-01 tariffs on imported kitchen cabinets benefit AMWD as a domestic manufacturer relative to Chinese-sourced competitors. But AMWD itself imports raw plywood from Vietnam, so the same tariffs hit AMWD's COGS — gross margin compression of 340-350bps in Q3 FY26 partly reflects this. This is the MOST SURPRISING NEW finding from the broader scrutiny: the original score did not flag the Vietnam plywood AD/CVD as a discrete refund-and-rolling-exposure issue. MODERATE because (a) honest disclosure, (b) refund is conditional on no petitioner appeal, (c) ongoing tariff exposure on imported components is real.
